content.value_statement: Genomic analysis often fails when file formats, indexes, and coordinate systems are handled inconsistently. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused pysam guidance for alignment, variant, sequence, and coverage workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to open and query SAM, BAM, and CRAM alignment files.
Shows region retrieval, pileup, read filtering, and coverage calculation patterns.
Guides VCF and BCF inspection, genotype access, filtering, and writing.
Covers FASTA, FASTQ, and tabix-indexed file workflows.
Documents common indexing requirements and coordinate system differences.
Provides integrated workflows combining BAM, VCF, BED, and FASTA data.
limitations: Does not include datasets, reference genomes, or benchmark files.
Does not validate clinical conclusions or variant pathogenicity.
Requires pysam, htslib-compatible files, and relevant index files in the user environment.
Examples assume local files and may need adaptation for production pipelines.

use_cases.title: Build alignment quality checks
use_cases.description: Create BAM or CRAM workflows that count reads, inspect flags, calculate coverage, and handle indexes correctly.

use_cases.title: Filter and summarize variants
use_cases.description: Work through VCF or BCF filtering, genotype access, INFO fields, FORMAT fields, and sample subsetting.

use_cases.title: Extract reference and read sequences
use_cases.description: Use FASTA, FASTQ, and tabix-indexed files to extract regions, convert formats, and prepare sequence summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Choose pysam objects
prompt_templates.prompt: I have BAM, VCF, FASTA, and FASTQ files. Explain which pysam classes I should use and when indexes are required.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a coverage check
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a pysam workflow to calculate per-base coverage for selected regions from an indexed BAM file.

prompt_templates.title: Filter variants safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through filtering a VCF by quality, depth, genotype, and allele frequency while preserving header information.

prompt_templates.title: Design an integrated pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a local pysam pipeline that validates VCF variants with BAM read support and extracts FASTA context sequences.

output_examples.input: Review a BAM file workflow for coverage across chr7:55000000-55200000.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering index checks, coordinate conversion, pileup or count_coverage selection, and summary metrics for depth review.

output_examples.input: Filter a VCF to high-quality variants and summarize sample genotypes.
output_examples.output: A stepwise filtering approach with quality thresholds, genotype handling notes, header preservation guidance, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Extract sequence context around variants using FASTA and VCF inputs.
output_examples.output: A local workflow that checks reference indexes, converts positions carefully, and reports context sequence handling decisions.

best_practices: Confirm coordinate conventions before mixing BAM, VCF, BED, and FASTA data.
Create and verify index files before using region-based queries.
Keep genomic data local when privacy, consent, or compliance requirements apply.
anti_patterns: Do not run examples on identifiable genomic data without access approval.
Do not assume VCF and pysam coordinate fields use the same indexing base.
Do not load large sequencing files into memory when streaming is sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill install pysam?
faq.answer: No. It explains installation commands and usage patterns. The user or environment must install dependencies.

faq.question: Which genomic formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers SAM, BAM, CRAM, VCF, BCF, FASTA, FASTQ, BED, GTF, GFF, and tabix-indexed files.

faq.question: Can it process real genomic files?
faq.answer: It can guide local code and analysis workflows. It does not include datasets or run tools by itself.

faq.question: Does it help with coordinate systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights 0-based pysam fields, 1-based VCF positions, and region string differences.

faq.question: Can it support private genomic data work?
faq.answer: Yes, when used with local files. Users should avoid sharing identifiable genomic data in prompts.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
